ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle ACD$ is the exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$, and $CE$ bisects $\angle ACD$. If $\angle A=70^\circ$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ECD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\angle A=70^\circ$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle A+\angle B=110^\circ$,\\
and since CE bisects $\angle ACD$,\\
we have $\angle ECD= \frac{1}{2}\angle ACD=\boxed{55^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, B, C, and D are on the same horizontal straight line, and BC extends rightward through C to D; A is above, with AB and AC connected; from C, ray CE is drawn to the upper right, located between CA and CD. The figure marks ∠A=70°, ∠B=40°, and near C marks an angle arc related to the exterior angle. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, ∠ACD is the exterior angle of △ABC at C. By the triangle exterior angle theorem, ∠ACD is equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, so ∠ACD=∠A+∠B=70°+40°=110°. Also because CE bisects ∠ACD, ∠ECD is half of ∠ACD, namely ∠ECD=110°÷2=55°.
